item: Which case each deposit falls in
why: The brief does not say where the money came from or whether tax was withheld. Every ladder below is a scale for one assumption, not a figure for this account.
what_would_settle_it: The Tax Payment Record set against the bank statement, deposit by deposit.

item: Surcharge when the payer failed to withhold
why: A 2004 reply from the tax administration says no surcharge is charged to the taxpayer or the payer. The 2018 law later gave the taxpayer a payment deadline of 30 June of the following year. No official text was found that says which one governs after that date. The 2004 reply was read on the Ministry of Commerce's database, not on the tax administration's own site.
what_would_settle_it: A written answer from the tax office in charge, or the tax administration's own copy of the reply showing its current status.

item: Whether the surcharge can exceed the tax
why: The collection law charges 0.05% a day with no ceiling. The Administrative Compulsion Law says a surcharge may not exceed the amount owed. No official text settling which applies to tax was read. The ladder uses the collection law as written, with no ceiling.
what_would_settle_it: A tax administration ruling or a court decision on this point, read on an official site.

why: The law sets 50% to 5 times the unpaid tax. Where inside that range a case lands is for the local tax office. Local penalty benchmarks were not read. The ladder shows both ends and no middle.
what_would_settle_it: The penalty decision itself, or the benchmark table published by the provincial tax bureau.

item: Income older than the look-back period
why: The law limits how far back tax can be recovered. Whether a tax office will still accept payment and issue a record for an older year, and whether a bank accepts money for which no record can be issued, was not found on any official page.
what_would_settle_it: Ask the tax office and the bank in writing.

item: The IRS page on late FBARs is gone
why: The IRS address for its Delinquent FBAR Submission Procedures (irs.gov/individuals/international-taxpayers/delinquent-fbar-submission-procedures) returned 'Page Not Found' on 11 November 2026, and the IRS options page lists three options without it. The Taxpayer Advocate Service page still states the no-penalty rule, and that is the page cited here.
what_would_settle_it: An IRS statement of where the procedure now lives, or that it was withdrawn.

item: Penalty under the Voluntary Disclosure Practice
why: The IRS published proposed new terms on 22 December 2025 and took comments until 22 March 2026. The page describes them as proposed. Whether they are final was not found, so no figure is shown for the willful route.
what_would_settle_it: The final IRS announcement, or Form 14457 instructions dated after the comment period.

item: U.S. tax and interest are not computed
why: They depend on the whole return for each year: other income, filing status, the foreign tax credit. Only the rates are given.
what_would_settle_it: A U.S. return prepared for each open year.

item: FBAR ceilings carry the January 2025 date
why: The federal regulation page, stated up to date as of 9 November 2026, still shows the table for penalties assessed on or after 17 January 2025. No 2026 adjustment appears there. The January 2025 figures are used.
what_would_settle_it: A later Federal Register notice, if one exists.

item: Amounts that make evasion a crime
why: The Criminal Law says 'relatively large' and 'huge' without figures. The judicial interpretation that sets the figures was not read.
what_would_settle_it: The Supreme People's Court and Supreme People's Procuratorate interpretation, read on an official site.

item: Which U.S. year the credit lands in
why: Chinese tax paid late is credited in the year it is paid unless an accrual choice was already made on a timely original return. If the U.S. taxed the income in an earlier year, the credit and the income may sit in different years, and the carryback is only one year. Whether that leaves tax paid twice depends on the return.
what_would_settle_it: A U.S. preparer, with the year of each Chinese payment and each U.S. return.

item: Repository review: the dashboard stops at 'the large number'
why: The dashboard's Tax page says unpaid Chinese tax 'is the large number' and the decision register marks 'What happens if the money was never taxed?' as answered with nothing missing. Neither mentions the daily surcharge, the fine range or the look-back periods.
what_would_settle_it: A link from those two places to this page.

item: Repository review: 'interest is exempt' is only the Chinese half
why: The dashboard's Tax page lists bank-deposit interest as exempt. That is the Chinese rule. Its U.S. rows do not say the same interest is taxable in the U.S., which decides whether the no-penalty FBAR route is open.
what_would_settle_it: One sentence on the dashboard's U.S. rows.
